help.intro: Aries keeps charts, techniques, tables, notes, and time navigation together in one retained professional workspace.
help.shortcutsIntro: This list follows the shortcuts active in the current app; obsolete desktop bindings are omitted.
help.shortcut.openSpotlightSeeded: Open Spotlight with the first digit
help.shortcut.contextualStep: Previous or next contextual time step
help.spotlightGettingStarted: Just start typing a date, time and place, then press Enter to create a chart. Smart Spotlight understands flexible date order—for example, 23 2 1583 or 1583 Feb 23—and accepts both 24-hour times such as 14:30 and AM/PM times such as 4pm.
help.gettingStartedBody: Use New to enter exact chart data, Open to choose a chart from a collection, or Here and Now for the current place and time.
help.workspaceBody: Charts and derived workflows stay open as documents in the sidebar. Switch documents without losing their state; use the Inspector, notes, chart context menus, and Spotlight to work across the active chart.
help.chartsBody: From a radix chart, open any subsidiary chart from the sidebar. Multiple charts can be nested.
help.timeBody: Arrow keys step the active chart on its natural time scale; Shift and Option/Alt select finer or alternate steps. Tab toggles the comparison ring, and the reset shortcut returns to the document's initial chart state.
help.tablesBody: Tables open inside the workspace and use the active chart. Use row actions to inspect or open dated results, and export supported tables as PDF or text. The sidebar is the current catalog of available tables.
help.researchBody: Time-lord and research work includes Firdaria, zodiacal releasing, decennials, circumambulations, triplicity directions, average returns, eclipses, fixed stars, and transit search where applicable.
help.settingsBody: Options control appearance, chart bodies and points, houses, aspects, dignities, orbs, ayanamsha, languages, corpus packs, and technique-specific calculation settings. Display-only changes refresh the visible chart without changing its astrology.
help.primaryDirectionsConcepts: Primary Directions direct a promissor toward a significator through a chosen model of the celestial sphere. Aries supports direct and converse motion, mundane and zodiacal directions, and selected aspects on either side of the direction.
help.primaryDirectionsSystems: Choose Placidus semi-arc, Placidus under-the-pole, Regiomontanus, Campanus, or Topocentric directions as appropriate to the method. The selected system also governs the related speculum and chart geometry.
help.primaryDirectionsSettings: Settings define promissors, significators, aspects, latitude and subzodiacal treatment, direct or converse calculation, static or dynamic keys, and the Moon's secondary motion. Presets are starting points and remain fully editable.
help.primaryDirectionsWorkflow: The Primary Directions document provides Radix, Annual, and Monthly ranges with age controls and live settings. Select a result to move the current cursor, inspect the event, open it in the chart, or export the list.
help.primaryDirectionsInChart: Directions in Chart can be celestial or terrestrial. Celestial views offer planet, ecliptic-foot, and full pseudo-astronomical projections; terrestrial views preserve the chosen mundane orientation. Comparison rings keep the radix visible beside the directed state.
help.filesBody: Chart collections are JSONL files stored in ~/Documents/Aries/Charts by default. Save and Save As write to the chosen collection; notes and exports remain separate.
